53:1: The people of interpretation differed regarding his statement, And the star when it goes down. Some of them said: What is meant by the star is the Pleiades, and what is meant by his statement, When it goes down, is when it falls. They said: The interpretation of the statement is: And the Pleiades when it falls. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And the star when it falls, he said: When the Pleiades fall with the dawn. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan: And the star when it goes down, he said: the Pleiades. Mujahid said: And the star when it goes down, he said: the fall of the Pleiades. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And the star when it goes down, he said, when it is set up. Others said: The meaning of this is: And the Qur’an when it is revealed. Who said that? Ziyad bin Abdullah Al-Hassani Abu Al-Khattab told me: Malik bin Sa’ir told us: Al-A’mash told us on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement, And the star when it goes down, he said: The Qur’an when it was revealed.
53:2: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the star, when it goes down, your companion has neither strayed nor gone astray. He said: Utbah ibn Abi Lahab said: I disbelieved in the Lord of the star. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you not fear that the dog of God will eat you? He said: So he went out on a trade trip to Yemen, and while they had camped, he heard the sound of a lion. He said to his companions: I am to be eaten. So they surrounded him and he struck their ears and they slept. Then he came and took him, and they heard nothing but his sound. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: And the star when it goes down. Then Ibn Abi Lahab, I think his name was Utbah, said: You have disbelieved in the Lord of the star. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Beware lest the dog of God eat you. He said: So he struck his head. He said: Ibn Tawus said on the authority of his father that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Are you not afraid that he will set his dog on you? So Ibn Abi Lahab went out with some people on a journey. When they were on a part of the road, they heard the roar of a lion. He said: It only wants me. So his companions gathered around him and put him in their midst. When they slept, the lion came and took him from among them. Some of the people of Basra who were knowledgeable in the Arabic language used to say: By the star he meant the stars. He said: He went with the singular form, but it has the meaning of the plural, and he supported his statement with the words of a camel herdsman. So she became a star in a quick puzzle in the hands of those who eat her frozen The correct statement in this regard, in my opinion, is what Mujahid said, that what he meant by the star in this place is Thuraya, because the Arabs call it the star. The statement made by the one from whom we narrated from the people of Basra is a statement that we do not know of any of the people of interpretation who said it, even if it has a basis, that is why we left saying it. And His statement, Your companion has neither strayed nor gone astray, God Almighty says: Your companion, O people, has not deviated from the truth nor has he departed from it, but he is on the right path and straight path. What he means by his saying and he did not go astray is that he did not become astray, but he is a righteous and sound person. It is said: he went astray, he goes astray from the word ghay which means to go astray, and ghawy is from to smell milk. And his saying your companion did not go astray is the answer to an oath by the star.
53:3: God Almighty says: Muhammad does not utter this Qur’an from his own desire.
53:4: It is only a revelation revealed. He says: This Qur'an is only a revelation from God revealed to him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Nor does he speak from [his own] inclination, meaning, he does not speak from his own inclination. It is only a revelation revealed, he said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, reveals to Gabriel, and Gabriel reveals to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: What he meant by his saying nor does he speak from [his own] inclination is inclination.
53:5: And His statement: He was taught this Qur'an by one of intense strength means the one of intense strength. What He meant by His statement intense strength is intense in causes. Qawwai is the plural of quwwa just as al-jathā is the plural of jathwa and al-hubba is the plural of hubwa. Some Arabs say: al-qawwai with a kasra on the qaf, just as arshwah is pluralized as arshā with a kasra on the ra' and al-hubwah with a damma on the ra'. It has been mentioned that the Arabs say: arshwah with a damma on the ra' and arshwah with a kasra. So the plural of the one who pluralizes that must be arshā with a kasra on the ra', according to the language of the one who says its singular is arshwah, and the plural of the one who pluralizes that must be arshā with a kasra on the ra', according to the language of the one who says arshwah in its singular form, and the plural of the one who pluralizes that must be damma on the ra', according to the language of the one who says arshwah in its singular form. And if the plural is with a kasra, then the one whose language is damma in the singular form, or with a damma, then the one who says kasr is used, then it is a matter of applying one of the two languages to the other. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement, He was taught by one of intense strength, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: He was taught by one of great strength, meaning Gabriel. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us on the authority of Abu Jaafar on the authority of Al-Rabi’: He was taught by the One of Mighty Power. He said: Gabriel, peace be upon him. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Abu Jaafar on the authority of Al-Rabi’, similarly.
53:6: And his saying, of a good character and then he rose up. The people of interpretation differed regarding his saying, of a good character. Some of them said: Its meaning is: of good character. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, of a beautiful appearance. He said: of a beautiful appearance. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: He who is tall and straight means he has a tall, handsome character. Others said that it means: powerful. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Of a time, He rose up means Of the strength is Gabriel. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan, Dhu Marra: He said: He has strength. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, Of a time, then He rose up: Of a time, he said: Of a time, strength. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakan told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’: Once he rose and rose means Gabriel, peace be upon him. The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of the one who said that the health of the body and its freedom from defects and ailments, and if the body is like this in a person, then he is strong. We only said that this is the case because the period is one of bitterness, and what is meant by it is: one with a healthy period. And if the period is healthy, then the person is healthy. From this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that charity is not permissible for a rich person or one with a healthy period.
53:7: And His statement, So He rose * while He was on the highest horizon, meaning: So this mighty and strong one rose and your companion Muhammad rose on the highest horizon. This was when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on a night journey, along with Gabriel, peace be upon them, at the highest point of the sunrise, which is the highest horizon. And He connected with His statement, And He, what is in His statement, So He rose from the mention of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And most of the speech of the Arabs, when they want to connect in a situation like this, is to show the allusion to the thing being connected to, so they say, He and so-and-so rose, and they rarely say, He and so-and-so rose. Al-Farra’ mentioned on the authority of some of the Arabs that he recited to him: Have you not seen that the spring hardens and becomes uneven? And the castor oil that is split The response of the castor oil to what is in the spring is equal to the mention of the spring and from it the saying of God If we were dust and our fathers Al-Ra’d 5 so he connected the fathers to the one referred to in we were without revealing we so likewise his saying and he rose up and it has been said: that the one who rose up is Gabriel, so if that is the case then there is no difficulty in that because his saying and he is from the mention of the name of Gabriel and it is as if the one who said that directed the meaning of his saying and he rose up: that is, he rose up and straightened. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Hakam told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’: Once he rose and rose means Gabriel, peace be upon him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And it is at the highest horizon. The horizon is that from which the day comes. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement, And He is on the highest horizon, he said: On the highest horizon of the East between them. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us on the authority of Abu Jaafar on the authority of Al-Rabi’: And he is at the highest horizon, meaning Gabriel. He said: Mihran told us on the authority of Abu Jaafar on the authority of Al-Rabi’: And he is in the highest horizon. He said: The highest heaven, meaning Gabriel, peace be upon him.
53:8: God Almighty says: Then Gabriel drew near to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and descended to him. This is from the deferred form, which means to bring it forward. Rather, it is then he descended, so he drew near, but it is good to bring forward the word drawn near, since drawing near indicates descending, and descending indicates drawing near, as it is said: So-and-so visited me, treated me well, and treated me well, so he visited me and cursed me, so he did wrong, and did wrong, so he cursed me, because harm is cursing, and cursing is harming. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan, Then he approached and came down. He said: Gabriel, peace be upon him. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, Then he approached and came down meaning: Gabriel. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, Then he approached and came down. He said: He is Gabriel, peace be upon him. Others said that the meaning of this is: Then the Lord approached Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and descended. Who said that? Yahya bin Saeed Al-Umawi told us, he said: My father told us, he said: Muhammad bin Amr told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, then he approached and descended. He said: His Lord approached and descended. Al-Rabi’ narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Bilal, on the authority of Sharik ibn Abi Namir, he said: I heard Anas ibn Malik telling us about the Night Journey of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that Gabriel ascended with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to the seventh heaven, then he ascended with him in a manner that no one knows but God until he came to the Lote Tree of the Limit. The Compeller, the Lord of Majesty, drew near and descended until he was two bow lengths away from it or nearer. Then God revealed to him whatever He willed, and God revealed to him whatever He willed, and God revealed to him, among what He revealed, fifty prayers upon his nation every day and night. And he mentioned the hadith.
53:9: And his saying, So he was two bow lengths away or nearer, meaning Gabriel was from Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the distance of two bow lengths away or nearer than that, meaning or closer to it. It is said, He was two bow lengths away from him, "He was two bow lengths away, He was two bow lengths away, He led two bow lengths away, and He was two bow lengths away." All of these mean: the distance of two bow lengths away. It was said: The meaning of his saying and he was two bow lengths away is that he was from it, as far as the string of the bow is. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, two bow lengths, he said: Where the string is on the bow. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan, He was two bow lengths away. He said, the distance of two bow lengths. Qatada said that. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid: He was two bow lengths away. He said: The distance or the length of two bow lengths. Abu Kurayb told us: Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Tahman, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah: He was two bow lengths away or nearer. He said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, approached him until he was the length of a cubit or two. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Razin: Two bow lengths. He said: It is not this bow length, but the length of two arms or less. And qab is the shackle. The commentators differed on the meaning of his statement, He was two bow lengths away or even nearer. Some of them said something similar to what we have said. Ibn Abi Al-Shawareb told us: Abd Al-Wahid bin Ziyad told us: Sulayman Al-Shaibani told us: Zur bin Hubaysh told us: Abdullah said regarding this verse, Then he was two bow lengths away or nearer, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, I saw Gabriel with six hundred wings. Abdul Hamid bin Bayan Al-Sakari told us: Khalid Abdullah told us, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, regarding his statement, He was two bow lengths away or nearer, he said: He saw Gabriel, peace be upon him, with six hundred wings in his form. Muhammad bin Ubaid told us: Qubaysah bin Laith Al-Asadi told us, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Razin Habish, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, He was two bow lengths away or nearer. He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel, peace be upon him, who had six hundred wings. Ibn Wakee’ narrated: Ibn Wahb narrated: Ibn Lahi’ah narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad on the authority of Urwah on the authority of Aishah who said: The first thing that happened to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was that he saw Gabriel (peace be upon him) in a dream in Ajyad. Then he went out to relieve himself and Gabriel shouted at him: O Muhammad, O Muhammad. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) looked right and left but saw nothing three times. Then he went out and saw him. Then he entered among the people. Then he went out, or he said: Then he looked - I doubt it - and saw him. This is what God said: “And the star when it goes down. Your companion has neither strayed nor erred. Nor does he speak from [his own] inclination.” Until His saying: Then he came down Gabriel to Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). And he was two bow lengths or nearer. He said: The length is half a finger’s length. Some of them said: Two cubits between them. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Zur ibn Hubaysh, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, and he was two bow lengths or nearer. He said: He had six hundred wings, meaning Gabriel, peace be upon him. Ibrahim bin Saeed told us: Abu Usamah told us: Zakariya told us, on the authority of Ibn Ashwa’, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Masruq, who said: I said to Aisha: What is the meaning of his statement, Then he approached and came closer * and was at a distance of two bow lengths or even nearer * and revealed to his servant what he revealed,? She said: That was Gabriel, who used to come to him in the form of men, but this time he came to him in his own form and blocked the horizon of the sky. Others said: Rather, the one who came two bow lengths or nearer was Gabriel from his Lord. Mention who said that Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, So he was two bow lengths away or nearer, he said: God from Gabriel, peace be upon him. Others said: Rather, what was two bow lengths away or nearer was: Muhammad from his Lord. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Ubayd al-Himyari, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, on the authority of some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: We said, ‘O Prophet of God, have you seen your Lord?’ He said, ‘I did not see Him with my eyes, but I saw Him with my heart twice.’ Then he recited, ‘Then He drew near and came closer.’ Khallad bin Aslam told us: Al-Nadr told us: Muhammad bin Amr bin Alqama bin Waqqas Al-Laithi told us, on the authority of Kathir, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When I was taken up, Gabriel went on until he came to Paradise. Then I entered and was given Al-Kawthar. Then he went on until he came to the Lote Tree of the Limit. Then your Lord drew near and descended until He was two bow lengths away or nearer. Then He revealed to His servant what He revealed.”
53:10: And his statement: Then He revealed to His servant what He revealed. The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that. Some of them said: Its meaning is that God revealed to His servant Muhammad His revelation, and they made his statement what He revealed mean the source. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Muadh bin Hisham told us: My father told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Then He revealed to His servant what He revealed, he said: His servant Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, what his Lord revealed to him. This interpretation of ma may be interpreted in two ways: one of them is that it means who and the meaning of the speech is He revealed to His servant which his Lord revealed to him. The other is that it means the source. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Muadh bin Hisham told us: My father told me on the authority of Qatada: Then He revealed to His servant what He revealed. Al-Hasan said: Gabriel. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi`: Then He revealed to His servant what He revealed. He said: On the tongue of Gabriel. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us on the authority of Abu Jaafar on the authority of Al-Rabi’, similarly. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement, Then He revealed to His servant what He revealed, that Gabriel revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what God revealed to him. The first of the two opinions on this matter, in our view, is the correct opinion of those who say: The meaning of this is: So Gabriel revealed to his servant Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, what his Lord revealed to him, because the opening of the speech occurred at the beginning of the surah with the report about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and about Gabriel, peace be upon him, and his saying, So he revealed to his servant what he revealed is in the context of that, and nothing came to indicate that the report was not about them, so that it is directed to what it was diverted to.
53:11: And His saying: The heart did not lie about what it saw. God Almighty says: Muhammad’s heart did not lie about what Muhammad saw, but rather it believed it. The people of interpretation differed about what his heart saw and did not deny. Some of them said: What his heart saw was the Lord of the Worlds. They said: He placed his sight in his heart, so he saw Him with his heart, but did not see Him with his eye. Who said that? Saeed bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: My uncle Saeed bin Abdul Rahman bin Saeed narrated to me, on the authority of Israel bin Yunus bin Abi Ishaq Al-Subaie, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, The heart did not lie about what it saw, he said: He saw it with his heart, may God bless him and grant him peace. Khallad bin Aslam told us: Al-Nadr bin Shumayl told us: Ibad, meaning Ibn Mansur, told us: I asked Ikrimah about His statement, The heart did not lie about what it saw. He said: Do you want me to tell you that it saw it? Yes, it saw it. Then it saw it, then it saw it, until its breath was cut off. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Isa bin Ubaid told us: I heard Ikrimah being asked, Did Muhammad see his Lord? He said, Yes, he saw his Lord. Yahya bin Wadh said: We were told by Salim, the freed slave of Muawiyah, on the authority of Ikrimah, similarly. Ahmad ibn Isa al-Tamimi narrated: Sulayman ibn Amr ibn Sayyar narrated: My father narrated to me, on the authority of Saeed ibn Zurbi, on the authority of Amr ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I saw my Lord in the most beautiful form, and He said to me: ‘O Muhammad, do you know what the highest assembly disputes about?’ I said: ‘No, O Lord.’ So He placed His hand between my shoulders, and I felt its coolness between my breasts, and I knew what was in the heavens and the earth, and I said: ‘O Lord, regarding degrees and expiations, and moving the feet to the Friday prayers, and waiting for the next prayer after the next.’ I said: ‘O Lord, You took Abraham as a friend, and You spoke directly to Moses, and You did this and that.’ He said: ‘Did I not expand your breast for you? Did I not remove your burden? Did I not do this to you? Did I not do that?’ He said: ‘Then He revealed to me things that I was not permitted to relate to you.’ He said: ‘That is what He said in His Book, relating to you: Then He drew near and came closer, and was two bow lengths away or nearer, and He revealed to His servant what He revealed: ‘The heart did not lie about what it saw.’ So He placed the light of my sight in my heart, and I looked at Him.’” With my heart Muhammad bin Amara and Ahmad bin Hisham told me: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Salih: The heart did not lie about what it saw. He said: He saw it twice with his heart. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Atiyah told us, on the authority of Qais Asim Al-Ahwal, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God chose Abraham with friendship, chose Moses with speech, and chose Muhammad with vision, may God’s prayers be upon them. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ziyad bin Al-Hussain, on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The heart did not lie about what it saw. He saw it with his heart. He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of someone who heard Ibn Abbas say: The heart did not lie about what it saw. He said: Muhammad saw his Lord. He said: It was narrated to us by Hakam on the authority of Abu Jaafar on the authority of Al-Rabi’: The heart did not lie. He did not lie about what he saw. He said: He saw his Lord. He said: Mihran told us on the authority of Abu Jaafar on the authority of Al-Rabi’: The heart did not lie about what it saw. He said: Muhammad saw his Lord with his heart. Others said: Rather, the one who saw him and did not deny him was Gabriel, peace be upon him. Who said that? Ibn Buzay` al-Baghdadi told me: Ishaq ibn Mansur told us, Israel said, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, on the authority of Abdullah, The heart did not lie about what it saw. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel wearing two fluttering garments, filling the space between heaven and earth. Ibrahim bin Yaqub Al-Jawzjani told us: Amr bin Asim told us: Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I saw Gabriel at the Lote Tree of the Limit, and he had six hundred wings, shaking out pearls and rubies from his feathers. Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i and Ibrahim bin Ya’qub told us: Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us that Al-Hussein bin Waqid told him: Asim bin Abi Al-Najud told me, on the authority of Abi Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, I saw Gabriel at the Lote Tree of the Limit, and he had six hundred wings. Al-Rafa’i added to his hadith: “I asked Asim about the wings, but he did not tell me. So I asked my companions, and they said: Each wing is between the east and the west.” Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, The heart did not deny what it saw, he said: He saw Gabriel in his form. He said: And he is the one who saw him in another descent. The reciters differed in their reading of the statement, The heart did not deny what it saw. The majority of the reciters of Medina, Mecca, Kufa, and Basra read it as kadhab with a light kafdh except for Asim al-Jahdari, Abu Ja`far al-Qari’, and al-Hasan al-Basri, who read it as kadhab with a shaddah, meaning that the heart did not deny what it saw, but rather made it true and honest. It is possible that its meaning, if read in this way, is The owner of the heart did not deny what it saw. We have explained the meaning of those who read it with a light kafdh The more correct of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who reads it with a light pronunciation, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it, and the other reading is not proven to be correct due to the correctness of its meaning.
53:12: The reciters differed in the reading of aftamarunhu. Abdullah bin Masoud and most of his companions read it as aftamarunhu with a fat-ha on the ta’ without an alif. This is the reading of most of the people of Kufa, and they directed its interpretation to aftajadunhu. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Hisham told us: Mughirah told us on the authority of Ibrahim that he used to read: aftamaruh with a fatha on the ta’ and without an alif, meaning: Do you deny him? And whoever read aftamaruh said: Do you argue with him? And the majority of the reciters of Medina, Mecca, and Basra, and some of the Kufians, read it as aftamaruh with a damma on the ta’ and the alif, meaning: Do you argue with him? The correct statement about this is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings. This is because the polytheists denied that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw what God showed him on the night of his Isra’, and they argued about that. So whichever of the two the reader recites is correct. The interpretation of the statement: Do you, O polytheists, argue with Muhammad about what he sees of the signs that God showed him?
53:13: And his saying: And he saw him on another occasion means: He saw him once again. The people of interpretation differed about who Muhammad saw in another descent, similar to their disagreement about his saying, The heart did not lie about what it saw. Mentioning some of the differences that were narrated about this. Mention of someone who said he saw Gabriel, peace be upon him: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated: Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi narrated: Dawud narrated from Amir from Masruq from Aisha that Aisha said: O Abu Aisha, whoever claims that Muhammad saw his Lord is the greatest slander against God. He said: I was reclining, then I sat up and said: O Mother of the Believers, give me time and do not rush me. Have you seen the words of God: And indeed, he saw him on another descent and And indeed, he saw him on the clear horizon (al-Takwir 81:23)? She said: It was Gabriel. He saw him once in his creation and the image in which he was created, and he saw him a second time when he descended from the heaven to the earth, his great creation filling the space between the heaven and the earth. She said: I was the first to ask the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about this verse. He said: It was Gabriel, peace be upon him. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday and Abd Al-A’la told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, with a similar chain of transmission. Yazid bin Harun told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, who said: I was with Aisha and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Wakee’ narrated: Abd Al-A’la narrated to us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said to him: O Abu Aisha, whoever claims that Muhammad saw his Lord has greatly slandered God. God says: No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision. (al-An’am 6:103) It is not for a human being that God should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a veil. (al-Shura 42:51) He said: I was reclining, then I sat up and said: O Mother of the Believers, wait and do not rush. Didn’t God say: And indeed, he saw him on another descent, and And indeed, he saw him on the clear horizon. (al-Takwir 81:23) She said: I was the first of this nation to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that, and he said: I have never seen Gabriel in his original form except on these two occasions, descending from the heaven, his great creation filling the space between the heaven and the earth. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ali told us: Dawud bin Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, who said: I was reclining with Aisha, and she said: O Abu Aisha, then he mentioned something similar. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud: And he saw him on another descent. He said: He saw Gabriel on a blanket that filled the space between heaven and earth. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qais bin Wahb, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Ibn Masoud: And indeed, he saw him on another descent. He said: He saw Gabriel in the fur of his feet like pearls, like rain on a plant. Al-Husayn bin Ali Al-Sada’i told me: Abu Usama told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qais bin Wahb, on the authority of Marra, regarding his statement, And he saw him on another occasion, then he mentioned something similar. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhayl, on the authority of Mujahid: And indeed he saw him on another occasion. He said: He saw Gabriel in his original form twice. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhail al-Hadrami, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: He saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his original form twice. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, And he saw him on another occasion. Gabriel, peace be upon him, said. Abdul Hamid bin Bayan narrated to us, he said: Muhammad bin Yazid narrated to us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Aamer, he said: Abdullah bin Al-Harith bin Nawfal narrated to me, on the authority of Ka’b, that he told him that God, the Blessed and Exalted, divided His vision and speech between Moses and Muhammad. Moses spoke to Him twice, and Muhammad saw Him twice. He said: Masruq came to Aisha and said: O Mother of the Believers, did Muhammad see his Lord? She said: Glory be to God, my hair stood on end when you said: Where are you in three things? Whoever narrated them to you has lied. Whoever informed you that Muhammad saw his Lord has lied. Then I recited: “No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision. And He is the Subtle, the Acquainted.” Al-An’am 6:103 And it is not for a human being that God should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a veil. Ash-Shura 42:51 And whoever informed you of what will happen tomorrow has lied. Then I recited the last verse of Surat Luqman 31:“Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour. He sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die.” Luqman 34 Whoever informed you that Muhammad concealed any of the revelation has... He lied, then she read, O Messenger, announce what has been revealed to you from your Lord (al-Ma’idah 5:67). She said, “But he saw Gabriel, peace be upon him, in his form twice.” Musa bin Abdul Rahman told us: Abu Usamah told us: Ismail told me on the authority of Amer: Abu Usamah told us: Ismail told me on the authority of Amer: Abdullah bin Al-Harith bin Nawfal told us: I heard Kaab, then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Abdul Hamid bin Bayan, except that he said in his hadith: Muhammad saw him once and Musa spoke to him twice. Mention of someone who said about him: He saw his Lord, the Almighty. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Amr bin Hammad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Samak bin Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: And indeed, he saw him on another descent. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw his Lord in his heart. A man said to him at that time: Is it not that vision cannot grasp Him, but He grasps all vision? (al-An’am 6:103). Ikrimah said to him: Do you not see the sky? He said: Yes. He said: Can all of it be seen? Saeed bin Yahya told us, he said: My father told us, he said: Muhammad bin Amr told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, And he had certainly seen him on another occasion * At the Lote Tree of the Limit, he said: His Lord drew near and came closer until he was two bow lengths away or nearer, and revealed to His servant what He revealed. He said: Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw him.
53:14: And His saying: at the lote tree of the farthest boundary God Almighty says: And he saw him at the lote tree of the farthest boundary, so at is a connection to His saying saw him and the lote tree is the jujube tree. It was called Sidrat al-Muntaha according to some of the commentators, because the knowledge of every scholar ends at it. Who said that? Ibn Humayd told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Hafs ibn Humayd, on the authority of Shammar, who said: Ibn Abbas came to Ka’b al-Ahbar and said to him: Tell me about the statement of God, Near the Lote Tree of the Limit * Near it is the Garden of Refuge. Ka’b said: It is a Lote Tree at the base of the Throne, to which the knowledge of every scholar ends, whether a close angel or a sent prophet. There is nothing behind it that is unseen, which none knows but God. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Jarir ibn Hazim told me, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Shamir ibn Atiyyah, on the authority of Hilal ibn Yasaf, who said: Ibn Abbas asked Ka’b about the Lote Tree of the Limit while I was present. Ka’b said: It is a Lote Tree over the heads of the bearers of the Throne, and to it the knowledge of creation ends, and beyond it there is no one’s knowledge. That is why it was called the Lote Tree of the Limit, because its summit ends. Others said: It is called the Lote Tree of the Limit, because that is where what descends from above it and what ascends from below it by the command of God ends. Who said that? Muhammad bin Anarah told me: Sahl bin Aamer told us: Malik told us, on the authority of Az-Zubayr, on the authority of Adi, on the authority of Talha Al-Yami, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the Lote Tree of the Limit, which is in the sixth heaven. Whoever ascends from the earth or from beneath it reaches it and is taken from it, and whatever descends from above it reaches it and is taken from it. Jaafar bin Muhammad Al-Marwazi told me, he said: Ya’la told us, on the authority of Al-Ajlah, he said: I said to Al-Dahhak: Why is it called the Lote Tree of the Limit? He said: Because everything that comes from God ends at it and does not go beyond it. Others said that it was called Sidrat al-Muntaha because everyone who follows the Sunnah and method of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ends up at it. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of al-Rabi`, regarding Sidrat al-Muntaha, he said: Everyone ends at it except for the Sunnah of Ahmad, and that is why it was called al-Muntaha. Ali bin Sahl told me, Hajjaj told us: Abu Jaafar Al-Razi told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah Al-Riyahi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah or someone else. Abu Jaafar Al-Razi was not sure. He said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the lote tree and it was said to him: This is the lote tree that everyone will reach except for your nation, following your way. The correct thing to say about this is that the meaning of al-Muntaha is the end, so it is as if it was said at the Lote Tree of the End. It is possible that it was called the Lote Tree of the End because the knowledge of every scholar of creation ends at it, as Ka’b said. It is possible that it was said that because what ascends from beneath it and descends from above ends at it, as was narrated on the authority of Abdullah. It is possible that it was said likewise because everyone who came after the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ends at it. It is possible that it was said that for all of that, and there is no report that cuts off the excuse that it was said for some of that and not for some of it, so there is no statement about it that is more correct than the statement that our Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, said, which is that it is the Lote Tree of the End. And with what we said about it being the jujube tree, the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, continued, and the people of knowledge said. Mentioning the effects and sayings of scholars: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I came to the lote tree, and its fruit was like jars, and its leaves were like the ears of elephants. When what God commanded covered it, it was transformed into rubies and emeralds and the like.” Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, on the authority of Malik ibn Sa’sa’ah, a man from his people, who said: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When I reached the seventh heaven, I came upon Abraham and said: ‘O Gabriel, who is this?’ He said: ‘This is your father Abraham.’ So I greeted him and he said: ‘Welcome to the righteous son and righteous prophet.’ Then the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary was raised up for me.” So the Prophet of God was told that its leaves were like the jars of Hajar and that its leaves were like the ears of elephants. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Khalid bin Al-Harith told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik bin Sa’sa’ah, a man from his people, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Muadh bin Hisham told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Anas bin Malik told us, on the authority of Malik bin Sa’sa’ah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned something similar. Ahmad bin Abi Surayj told us, he said: Al-Fadl bin Anbasa told us, he said: Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit Al-Bunani, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I rode Al-Buraq, and it took me to the Lote Tree of the Limit. Its leaves were like the ears of elephants, and its fruit was like jugs. He said: Then, when what God commanded covered it, it changed, and no one can describe its beauty. He said: Then God revealed to me what He revealed.” Ahmad bin Abi Surayj told us, he said: Abu Al-Nadr told us, he said: Salman bin Al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Anas, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Angel ascended with me. Then I reached the lote tree and I knew that it was a lote tree. I knew its leaves and its fruit. Then when what God commanded covered it, it was transformed until no one could describe it.” Muhammad bin Sinan Al-Qazzaz told us, Yunus bin Ismail told us, Sulayman told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the same, except that he said until I cannot describe it. Ali bin Sahl narrated: Hajjaj narrated: Abu Ja`far al-Razi narrated: al-Rabi` bin Anas narrated: Abu al-`Aliyah al-Riyahi narrated: Abu Hurayrah or someone else - Abu Ja`far al-Razi was not sure - said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the lote-tree and it was said to him: This lote-tree is the place where everyone from your nation will reach according to your way. Then, behold, it is a tree from whose root spring rivers of water unaltered, rivers of milk whose taste never changes, rivers of wine delicious to those who drink, and rivers of pure honey. It is a tree in whose shade a rider can travel for seventy years without crossing it, and its leaves cover the entire nation. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhail al-Hadrami, on the authority of al-Hasan al-Arni, I think it was on the authority of al-Hudhayl ibn Shurahbil, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud: The Lote Tree of the Limit he said: Whoever is patient with Paradise on it or on it, or on it, the excess of fine silk and brocade, or places excess on it. Ibn Hamid told us about it again on the authority of Mihran, who said on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Arni, on the authority of Al-Hudhayl, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, and he did not doubt it, and he added to it, he said, The patience of Paradise, meaning its middle. He also said, On it are the excess of fine silk and brocade. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhail, on the authority of al-Hasan al-Arni, on the authority of al-Hudhayl ibn Shurahbil, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Masoud, regarding his statement, The Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, he said: It is the tree of Paradise, upon which are brocade and heavy silk. Abu Kurayb told us: Yunus bin Bakir told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Yahya bin Ibad bin Abdullah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Asma bint Abi Bakr, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mention the Lote Tree of the Limit and say: One hundred riders will travel in the shade of its branches, or he said: One rider will seek shade in its branches. Yahya was unsure: It has golden beds, as if its fruit were jars. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of al-Rabi`, At the Lote Tree of the Limit. He said: The Lote Tree is a tree in whose shade a rider can travel for a hundred years without crossing it, and even if one of its leaves covers the entire nation. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary was raised up for me in the seventh heaven. Its fruit is like the jars of Hajar, and its leaves are like the ears of elephants. From its trunk come forth two apparent rivers and two hidden rivers. I said to Gabriel, What are these two rivers? They are spirits. He said, As for the two hidden rivers, they are in Paradise, and as for the two apparent rivers, they are the Nile and the Euphrates.
53:15: And His saying, Near it is the Garden of Refuge, God Almighty says: Near the Lote Tree of the Limit is the Garden of Refuge for the martyrs. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas: His statement, Near it is the Garden of Refuge, he said: It is to the right of the Throne and it is the abode of the martyrs. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Near them is the Garden of Refuge. He said: It is like His saying: For them are the Gardens of Refuge as a reward for what they used to do. (Al-Sajdah: 19). Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Near it is the Garden of Refuge, he said: The dwellings of the martyrs.
53:16: And His saying, When that which covers the lote tree covers it, God Almighty says: And indeed he saw him on another descent, when that which covers the lote tree covers it. Then behold, he saw him from afar. The interpreters differed about what covered the lote tree. Some of them said: It was covered by a layer of gold. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said: Sahl bin Aamer told us, he said: Malik told us, on the authority of Al-Zubayr bin Adi, on the authority of Talha Al-Yami, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah: When that which covers the lote tree covers it, he said: It was covered by a moth of gold. Abu Kurayb told us: Abu Khalid told us, on the authority of Jubayr, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I saw it with my own eyes, the lote tree of the farthest boundary, until I verified it, then a golden curtain stood in the way of it. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Jubayr, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, When that which covers the lote tree covers it, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I saw it until I verified it, then a bed of gold stood in the way of it. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Mujahid and Ibrahim, regarding his statement, When that which covers the lote tree covers it, they said: It was covered by a layer of gold. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Musa, meaning Ibn Ubaydah, on the authority of Yaqub ibn Zayd, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked: What did you see covering the lote tree? He said: I saw it covered with a moth of gold. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, When that which covers the lote tree covers it, he said: It was said to him, O Messenger of God, what did you see covering that lote tree? He said: I saw it covered by a moth of gold, and I saw on every leaf an angel standing, glorifying God. Others said: The one who covered it was the Lord of Glory and His angels. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, When that which covers the lote tree covers it, he said, God covered it, and Muhammad saw one of the greatest signs of his Lord. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, When that which covers the lote tree covers it, he said: The branches of the lote tree were pearls and rubies or emeralds, and Muhammad saw them, and Muhammad saw his Lord in his heart. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of al-Rabi`, When that which covers the lote tree covers it, he said: The light of the Lord covered it, and the angels covered it out of love for God, like crows when they land on trees. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us on the authority of Abu Ja`far on the authority of al-Rabi`, something similar. Ali bin Sahl told us: Hajjaj told us: Abu Jaafar Al-Razi told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah Al-Riyahi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah or someone else. Abu Jaafar was unsure. He said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the lote tree. He said: The light of the Creator covered it, and the angels covered it like crows when they land on trees. Then he said: Ask him.
53:17: God Almighty says: His sight did not deviate to the right or to the left from what he saw, meaning, nor did it exceed what he was commanded to do, meaning: It rose above the limit that was set for it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, His sight did not swerve, nor did it go beyond what it was commanded to do. He said, It did not swerve to the right or to the left, nor did it go beyond what it was commanded to do. Our grandfather Ibn Hamid said: Mihran told us on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi, His sight did not swerve nor did it go astray. He said that he saw Gabriel in the form of an angel. He said: Thabit Mahran, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: His sight did not swerve nor did it go beyond the bounds. He said: It did not swerve: it went right or left, nor did it go beyond the bounds.
53:18: And his saying, He certainly saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord, God Almighty says: Muhammad saw there some of the greatest signs and evidence of his Lord. The interpreters differed regarding these great verses. Some of them said: He saw a green leaf that covered the horizon. Who said that? Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us: Abu Mu’awiyah told us: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah: He has certainly seen of the greatest signs of his Lord. He said: A green leaf from Paradise that filled the horizon. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Abdullah said, and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Ibn Masoud: Among the greatest signs of his Lord he said: A green leaf that filled the horizon. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-A’mash, that Ibn Mas’ud said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a green blanket from Paradise that filled the horizon. Others said: He saw Gabriel in his true form. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd, regarding his statement, He has certainly seen of the greatest signs of his Lord, said: Gabriel saw him in his creation in the heavens, the distance between him and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
53:19: God the Most High says: Have you considered, O polytheists, Al-Lat? It is from God, and the letter taa was added to it, making it feminine, just as it is said ‘Amr for the male and ‘Umra for the female, and just as it is said for the male ‘Abbas, then it is said for the female ‘Abbasa. Thus the polytheists named their idols with the names of God the Most High and His names are sanctified. They said: From God is Al-Lat, and from the Almighty is Al-‘Uzza. They claimed that they are the daughters of God. God is exalted above what they say and fabricate. So God the Most High said to them: Have you considered, O you who claim that Al-Lat, Al-‘Uzza, and Manat, the third, are the daughters of God? Do you have the male? He says: Do you choose for yourselves a male from among your children and dislike a female for her and assign for Him a female whom you would not like for yourselves, but you kill her out of your dislike for them. The reciters differed regarding his saying: Al-Lat. The majority of the reciters of the regions recited it with a light ta’, according to the meaning that I described. It was mentioned that Al-Lat was a house in Nakhalah that was worshipped by the Quraysh. Some of them said: It was in Taif. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-Uzza? As for Al-Lat, it was in Taif. Yunus told me: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-Uzza? He said: Al-Lat was a house in a palm tree that the Quraysh worshipped. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Abu Saleh read it as Al-Lat with a shaddah on the ta and made it an attribute of the idol that they worshipped. They said: He was a man who mixed gruel for the pilgrims, and when he died, they devoted themselves to his grave and worshipped it. The report was mentioned by the one who said it: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza? He said: He used to mix gruel for the pilgrims, so he devoted himself to his grave. He said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, Have you seen Al-Lat? He said: Al-Lat used to knead gruel for the pilgrims. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, Al-Lat said: He used to mix gruel, then he died, so they devoted themselves to his grave. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Al-Lat, he said: A man used to mix gruel for the polytheists, then he died, so they devoted themselves to his grave. Ahmad bin Hisham told us: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Saleh, regarding his statement, Al-Lat, he said: Al-Lat was the one who was in charge of their gods, mixing gruel for them, and he was in Taif. Ahmad bin Yusuf told me: Abu Ubaid told us: Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Abu al-Ashhab, on the authority of Abu al-Juza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: He used to mix gruel for the pilgrims. The first of the two readings that is more correct in our view is the reading of the one who read with a light ta’, based on the meaning that was described to the reader, as well, due to the consensus of the proof from the readers of the regions. Some of them said: They were trees that they worshipped. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: And al-Uzza. He said: al-Uzza is a tree. Others said: Al-Uzza was a white stone. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaafar, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: Al-Uzza is a white stone. Others said: It was a house in Taif that was worshipped by Thaqif. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And Al-Uzza, that Al-Uzza was a house in Taif that the Thaqif worshipped. Others said it was in Batn Nakhal. Who said that?
53:20: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And Manat is the third other. He said: As for Manat, it was the dried-up gods that they used to worship, meaning Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, and Manat. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement, And Manat, the third, the other, he said: Manat was a house in Al-Mushallal that the Banu Ka’b worshipped. The Arabists differed on the reason for stopping at Al-Lat and Manat. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: If you are silent, you say Al-Lat. Likewise, Manat, you say: Manat. He said: Some of them said: Al-Lat, so he made it from Al-Lat, so he made it from Al-Lat which is yalta, and the language of the Arabs is that they stop at what has the Haa with the Taa, they say: I saw Talhat, and everything that is written, they stop at it with the Taa, like the blessing of your Lord and the tree. Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to stop at Al-Lat with the Haa, Have you seen Al-Lat? Others of them used to say: The choice in everything that is not added is to be with the Haa, mercy from my Lord and a tree that comes out, and what is added is permissible with the Haa and the Taa, so the Taa is for the addition and the Haa because it is singular and stopped at, unlike the second. This third statement is the most widespread of the languages and most of them among the Arabs, even though the other has a known aspect. Some of the people of knowledge of the speech of the Arabs from the people of Basra used to say: Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, and Manat are the third, idols of stone that were inside the Kaaba and they worshipped them.
53:21: And his saying, Do you have the male and He has the female? He says: Do you claim that you have the male that you are satisfied with and God has the female that you are not satisfied with for yourselves?
53:22: That is indeed an unfair division. God Almighty says: This division of yours is an unfair, unequal, deficient, and incomplete division, because you have attributed to your Lord children that which you dislike for yourselves, and you have preferred for yourselves what pleases you. The Arabs say, Darruh haqquhu with a kasra on the ḍād, and ḍazzuh with a ḍamma on the ḍād, so I deprive him and I deprive him, and that is if I deprive him of his right and prevent him from it. I was told on the authority of Muammar ibn al-Muthanna, who said, Al-Akhfash recited to me: If you turn away from us, we will disparage you, and if you are absent, your arrow will be pierced and your nose will be swollen. Some Arabs say dhizi with a fatha on the dad and without the hamza, and some say dhaazi with a fatha and hamza, and dhuzai with a damma and hamza. No one recited any of these languages. As for dhizi with a kasra, it is fa’la with a damma on the fa’. The dad was broken in it as it was broken in their saying qawm bayd and ‘ayn, which is a verb because its singular is bayda’ and ‘ayna’, to combine the plural, the two, and the one. Likewise, they disliked the damma of dhizi, so you say dawza for fear that it would become with a waw, which is from the ya’. Al-Farra’ said: I decided on the damma of the first letter because the feminine adjectives come either with a fatha or a damma, so the fatha is sakra sakra and ’asha thirsty, and the damma is the female and the pregnant. So if it is a noun and not an adjective, its first letter is broken, like his saying, And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers (al-Dhariyat 51:55). Its first letter is broken because it is a noun and not an adjective. Likewise, al-Shi’ra poetry has a kasra at the beginning because it is a noun and not an adjective. In a similar manner to what we said in the interpretation of his statement, an unfair division, he said: The people of interpretation, although their wording differed in expressing it, some of them said: a crooked division. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: That is indeed a division that is unfair, he said: Crooked. Others said it was an unfair division. Bishr told us: Yazid told us that Saeed was killed, on the authority of Qatada: That is an unfair division. He said: An unjust division. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: An unfair division means an unjust division. Muhammad bin Hafs Abu Ubaid Al-Wasa’i told us: Ibn Hamid told us: Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Ibn Umrah, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, That would be an unfair division, he said: That would be a permissible division in which there is no right. Others said: It is an incomplete division. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan: That is an unfair division. He said: It is incomplete. Others said: A contrary division. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd, regarding his statement, That is indeed an unfair division, said: They attributed daughters to God, the Blessed and Exalted, and they attributed daughters to the angels of God and worshipped them. He recited, Or has He taken from what He creates daughters and preferred you with sons? And when He gives you good tidings? Az-Zukhruf 43:16-17. He recited, And they attribute daughters to God An-Nahl 16:57 to the end of the verse. He said: They ascribe to God a son as the Jews and Christians did. He recited, Thus said those before them Al-Baqarah 2:118. He said: In the speech of the Arabs, the unfair division means: opposition. He recited, They are only names which you have named, you and your fathers.
53:23: God Almighty says: These names that you have named, namely Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other, are nothing but names that you and your fathers, O polytheists, have named, and your fathers before you. God has not sent them down meaning by these names He says: God has not permitted that to you nor has He given you permission to do it. Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement, of authority...to the end of the verse. And His statement, They follow nothing but conjecture, God Almighty says: These polytheists follow nothing in these names by which they named their gods except conjecture that what they say is true, not certainty. And what their souls desire, He says: And their own desires, because they did not take that from a revelation that came to them from God, nor from a Messenger of God who informed them of it. Rather, it is a breach from their own selves, or they took it from their fathers who were disbelieving in God just as they are. And His statement, And indeed there has come to them from their Lord guidance, means: And indeed these polytheists have come from their Lord to clarify what they are uncertain about, and that is their naming of al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat the third with these names and their worship of them. He says: Indeed there has come to them from their Lord guidance in that and clarification by the revelation that We revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that they should not be worshipped and that worship is only appropriate for God, the One, the Compeller. Ibn Zayd said about this: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: And there has certainly come to them guidance from their Lord, but they did not benefit from it.
53:24: God Almighty says: Or did Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, desire what God gave him of this honor with which He honored him of prophethood and messengership and sent down revelation to him and wished for that, so his Lord gave it to him? To God belongs whatever is in the Hereafter and in this world. He gives to whomever He wills of His creation whatever He wills and withholds from whomever He wills of them whatever He wills. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement, Or does man have what he desires? He said, And if Muhammad desired this, then that is his right.
53:25: God Almighty says: To God belongs the Hereafter and the first.
53:26: And His statement, And how many are there angels in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all? God Almighty says: And how many are there angels in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all with God for those for whom they intercede, unless they intercede for him after God has given them permission to intercede for whomever He wills among them to intercede for and is pleased with. He says: And after He is pleased with His angels who intercede for him to intercede for him, so that their intercession will then benefit him. This is only a rebuke from God Almighty to His idol worshippers and the leaders of Quraysh and others who used to say, We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to God. (al-Zumar 39:3). So God Almighty said to them: The intercession of My angels who are with Me will not benefit those for whom they intercede except after My permission for them to intercede for him and My pleasure, so how about the intercession of those besides them? So He informed them that the intercession of those they worship besides Him will not benefit them.
53:27: God Almighty says: Those who do not believe in the resurrection in the Hereafter, and that is on the Day of Resurrection, call the angels of God by female names. This is because they used to say: They are the daughters of God. And in a similar manner to what we said about his statement, Naming the female, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Sumayyah the female, he said: females.
53:28: And His statement: And they have no knowledge of it God Almighty says: And they have no knowledge of what they say about calling the angels female names. They follow nothing but conjecture. He says: They follow nothing in that except conjecture, meaning that they say that based on conjecture without knowledge. His saying, And suspicion does not replace the truth at all, means that suspicion does not replace the truth at all, so it can take its place.
53:29: And His saying, So turn away from whoever turns away from Our remembrance, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So leave, O Muhammad, whoever turns away from the remembrance of God and does not believe in Him and declare His Oneness. His saying, And he only wanted the life of this world, means that he did not seek what is with God in the Hereafter, but rather he sought the adornments of this worldly life and sought to remain in it.
53:30: God Almighty says: What these people who do not believe in the Hereafter say about the angels, by calling them female names, their level of knowledge means they have no knowledge other than this disbelief in God and associating partners with Him based on conjecture without certain knowledge. Ibn Zayd used to say about this: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, “So turn away from whoever turns away from Our remembrance and desires only the life of this world. That is the extent of their knowledge.” He said: He says that they have no knowledge except that which they are in of disbelief in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their plotting against what came from God. He said: And these are the people of polytheism. And His statement: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is guided. God Almighty says: Indeed, your Lord, O Muhammad, is most knowing of who has deviated from His way in His previous knowledge and does not believe, and that way is Islam. And He is most knowing of who is guided. He says: And your Lord is most knowing of who has found his way and followed it in His previous knowledge, and that way is also Islam.
53:31: God Almighty says: “And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He sends astray whom He wills, and He is most knowing of them. “That He may reward those who do evil for what they have done.” That is, to reward those of His creation who disobeyed Him and did evil by disobeying Him, and He will reward them with the Fire for it. And He may reward those who do good with good. That is, to reward those who obeyed Him and did good by obeying Him in this world with good, which is Paradise, and He will reward them with it. It was said: He meant by that the people of polytheism and faith. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Abdullah bin Ayyash told me: Zaid bin Aslam said about the statement of God, That He may reward those who do evil for what they have done and reward those who do good Al-Mu’minun.
53:32: And His statement, Those who avoid the major sins, means: Those who stay away from the major sins that God has forbidden and prohibited for them, so they do not approach them. This is associating partners with God, and what we have explained in His statement, If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden, We will remove from you your lesser sins. (An-Nisa’: 31). His saying: And indecencies are adultery and the like, for which God has imposed a punishment. And his saying: Except for a few. The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of except in this place. Some of them said: It means a discontinuous exception. They said: The meaning of the statement is: Those who avoid major sins and indecencies except for the few sins and indecencies that they committed in the pre-Islamic era, for God has forgiven them for it and will not hold them accountable for it. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except minor ones, meaning: except what has already happened. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except for the minor ones, he said: The polytheists were only working with us yesterday, so God, the Almighty, revealed, except for the minor ones, which refers to what they did in the pre-Islamic era. He said: The minor ones are the major sins and immoralities that they committed in the pre-Islamic era before Islam, and He forgave them for them when they converted to Islam. Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ayyash, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Muhammad, who said: A man asked Zayd ibn Thabit about this verse: Those who avoid major sins and immoralities, except minor ones, so he said: God has forbidden you immoralities, both apparent and secret. Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Abdullah bin Ayyash told me: Zaid bin Aslam said about the statement of God, Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except minor sins, he said: The major sins of polytheism and immoralities, such as adultery, were abandoned when they entered Islam, so God forgave them for what they had committed and committed of that before Islam. Some of the people of knowledge of the Arabic language directed the interpretation of except in this place to this aspect that I mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said in his interpretation of that: They were not given permission to touch something that is not from the indecencies nor from the major sins. And something may be excepted from something that is not from it on the basis of a pronoun that has been refrained from, so it is a metaphor: except that he touches something that is not from the indecencies nor from the major sins. The poet said: A town that has no companions except the camels and the wild donkeys Al-Ya'afir: the gazelles and Al-Ays: the camels, and they are not people, so it is as if he said: It has no companions except that it has gazelles and camels. Some of them said: Al-Ya'afir is the red gazelle and Al-Ays is the white one. A group of interpreters said something similar to this. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, that Ibn Mas’ud said: The fornication of the eyes is looking, the fornication of the lips is kissing, the fornication of the hands is touching, and the fornication of the feet is walking. The private parts confirm or deny that. If he comes forward with his private parts, then he is a fornicator, otherwise it is a lick. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar, who said: Ibn Tawus told us on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I have never seen anything more resembling a lick than what Abu Hurayrah said on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “God has decreed for the son of Adam his share of fornication, and it will inevitably overtake him. The fornication of the eyes is looking, and the fornication of the tongue is speech. The soul desires and longs, and the private parts confirm or deny that.” Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, regarding his statement, Except for a small amount, he said: If it comes beforehand, it is adultery, and if it comes afterward, it is a small amount. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Mansour bin Abd al-Rahman told us: I asked al-Sha’bi about the statement of God, They avoid major sins and immoralities, except minor sins. He said: It is less than adultery. Then he mentioned to us on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: Adultery of the eyes is what you look at, adultery of the hand is what you touch, adultery of the foot is what you walk, and intercourse with the private parts. Muhammad ibn Muammar told me: Ya`qub told us: Wahib told us: Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khathim ibn Amr al-Qari told us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Nafi`, who is called Ibn Lubabah at-Ta`ifi, told us: I asked Abu Hurayrah about the statement of God, Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except minor sins. He said: Kissing, winking, looking, and intimate contact. If circumcision touches circumcision, then ritual ablution is required, which is adultery. Others said: Rather, this is a valid exception, and the meaning of the statement is: Those who avoid major sins and indecencies, except for minor sins, unless he commits them and then repents. Who said that? Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Abu Asim told us: Zakariya ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except minor sins. He said: It is a man who commits an immoral act and then repents. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you forgive, O God, you forgive many, and which servant of yours is there who does not forgive? Ibn Al-Muthanna told me: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, that he said: In this verse, except for the touch, he said: the one who touches the sin and then abandons it. And the poet said: If you forgive, O God, you forgive a lot, and which servant of yours is there without pain? Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie’ told me: Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who I think traced it back to the Prophet: Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except minor sins. He said: The minor sin is adultery, then he repents and does not return to it, and the minor sin is theft, then he repents and does not return to it, and the minor sin is drinking alcohol, then he repents and does not return to it. He said: That is the minor sin. Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding the statement of God, Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except minor sins, he said, The minor sins are adultery, theft, or drinking alcohol, then one does not do it again.
