Yaqoub told me: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding the statement of God, Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except minor sins, he said, The minor sins are adultery, theft, or drinking alcohol, then one does not do it again. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement, Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except minor sins, he said: The companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: This man commits a minor sin, such as fornication or drinking alcohol, but he conceals it and then repents from it. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Except for a touch. He touches it at once. I said: Adultery. He said: Adultery then he repents. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us: Muammar said: Al-Hasan used to say about the limmah: A man may limmah to an immoral act and then repent. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Saleh, who said: Adultery, then he repents. He said: It was narrated to us by Mihran on the authority of Abu Jaafar on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Al-Hasan: Except for a small amount. He said: That the incident occurs and then it stops. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Al-Lammam means the one who touches something once. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said: Yahya ibn Ayoub told me on the authority of Al-Muthanna ibn Al-Sabah on the authority of Amr ibn Shuaib that Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Al-As said: The minor sin is less than polytheism. Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Amer told us: Marra told us on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Qasim regarding his statement, except for a small amount of sin, he said: A small amount of sin is committed. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Except for a touch, he said: A man touches a sin and then abandons it. He said: The people of the Age of Ignorance used to circumambulate the House and they would say: If you forgive, O God, we will forgive many. And which of your servants is there who has no pain? Others who directed the meaning except for the discontinuous exception said: The slightest thing is less than the limit of this world and the limit of the hereafter, and God has overlooked it. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn al-Zubayr: Except for a small amount. He said: What is between the two limits, the limit of this world and the torment of the Hereafter. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: Al-Lammam is what is less than the two limits, the limits of this world and the hereafter. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Utaybah, he said: Ibn Abbas said: Al-Lammam is what is less than the two limits, the limit of this world and the limit of the hereafter. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Those who avoid major sins and immoralities, except minor sins, he said: Everything between the two limits, the limit of this world and the limit of the Hereafter, is expiated by prayers, and it is the minor sin, and it is less than every obligatory sin. As for the limit of this world, it is every limit whose punishment God has imposed in this world. As for the limit of the Hereafter, it is everything that He seals with the Fire and postpones its punishment until the Hereafter. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Zaid, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, except for a small amount, he said: What is between the two limits is every sin for which there is no limit in this world or punishment in the hereafter, then it is a small amount. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Those who avoid major sins and immoralities, except minor ones. Minor ones are those that are between the two extremes and do not reach the limit of this world or the limit of the Hereafter, and are deemed obligatory by God for its people to be in Hell, or are immoral and are punishable by the punishment in this world. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Mihran, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Some of them said that the lamm is what is between the two limits and the limit of the hereafter. Abu Kurayb and Yaqub told us: Ismail bin Ibrahim told us: Saeed bin Abi Aruba told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The touch is what is between the two limits, the limit of this world and the limit of the hereafter. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan, who said: Ad-Dahhak said: Except for a small amount of sin. He said: Everything between the limits of this world and the hereafter is a small amount of sin, which God forgives. The first and most correct of the sayings in this regard, in my opinion, is the saying of those who said that except means a discontinuous exception, and the meaning of the statement is directed to those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except minor sins, meaning less than the major sins and less than the immoralities that warrant the prescribed punishments in this world and punishment in the Hereafter, for that is pardoned for them. In my opinion, this is similar to the saying of God, the Most High, If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden, We will remove from you your lesser sins and admit you to a noble entrance. (An-Nisa’: 31). God, the Most High, promised that by avoiding the major sins, pardon for lesser sins is the minor sins about which the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The eyes adorn themselves, the hands adorn themselves, the feet adorn themselves, and the private parts confirm or deny that. This is because there is no prescribed punishment for anything less than the vagina entering the private parts, and that is God’s pardon for the punishment of the servant for it, and God, the Most High, is too generous to return to what He has pardoned. This is God’s pardon in this world for the punishment of the servant for it, and God, the Most High, is too generous to return to what He has pardoned, as was narrated. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the word lamm in the speech of the Arabs: is close to something. Al-Farra’ mentioned that he heard the Arabs say: A strike that is close to killing, meaning a strike close to killing. He said: I heard from another, Did he not do something? meaning: He almost did something. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Indeed, your Lord, O Muhammad, is vast in forgiveness. His forgiveness is vast for sinners whose sins do not reach the level of heinousness and major sins. God Almighty only informs His servants by saying this that He forgives minor sins, including those we have described, for those who avoid major sins and heinousness. Yunus told us: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, Indeed, your Lord is Vast in forgiveness, that He forgave them for that. And His statement, He knows you best when He created you from the earth, means, the Most High, the Majestic, says: He knows best who among you is a believer from an unbeliever, who does good from evil, and who is obedient from a disobedient, when He originated you from the earth and created you from it by creating your father Adam from it, and when you were fetuses in the wombs of your mothers, meaning, when you were fetuses not yet born, and yourselves after you had become men and women. In a similar manner to what we said about that, he said: Is the interpretation? Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, He is most knowing of you when He created you from the earth, he said, It is similar to His statement, ‘And He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided’ Al-An’am 117- Al-Nahl 125- Al-Qasas 56- Al-Qalam 7. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, When He created you from the earth, he said: When He created Adam from the earth, then He created you from Adam, and he recited, And when you were fetuses in the wombs of your mothers. We have previously explained the meaning of the fetus and why it was called a fetus, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. And His saying, So do not claim yourselves to be pure, means that He, the Most High, says: So do not testify that yourselves are pure and free from sins and transgressions. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan who said: I heard Zaid bin Aslam say: Do not claim yourselves to be pure, meaning: do not acquit yourself. And His saying, He knows best who fears Him, means that God Almighty says: Your Lord, O Muhammad, knows best who among His servants fears God’s punishment and avoids His disobedience.
53:33: God Almighty says: Have you seen, O Muhammad, the one who turned away from faith in God and turned away from Him and His religion and gave his companion a little of his wealth and then withheld from him and did not give him anything, so he was miserly with him? It was mentioned that this verse was revealed about Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira because some of the polytheists rebuked him. He had followed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his religion, so the one who rebuked him guaranteed that if he gave him some of his money and returned to his polytheism, he would bear the punishment of the Hereafter on his behalf. So he did so, and he gave the one who rebuked him for that some of what he had guaranteed him, then he was stingy with him and prevented him from the full amount he had guaranteed him. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, and he was steadfast, Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira said, He gave a little, then he was steadfast. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about the statement of God, Have you seen him who turns away? until the statement, so he sees? He said: This is a man who had become Muslim and was met by someone who was taunting him. He said: You have abandoned the religion of the elders and led them astray and claimed that they are in the Fire. It was incumbent upon you to support them, but what will be the case with your fathers? He said: I feared the punishment of God. He said: Give me something and I will bear every punishment that was upon you. So he gave him something. He said: Give me more. So he struggled until he gave him something and wrote him a letter and bore witness for him. This is the statement of God, Have you seen him who turns away and is given little and is hard-pressed? “Does he have knowledge of the unseen so he sees?” This verse was revealed concerning him. And Binjo, whom we mentioned in the meaning of his saying and he emphasized, said the people of interpretation. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan al-Shaibani, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He gave a little and then stopped. He said: He gave a little and then stopped. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Have you seen he who turns away and gives little and is stingy? He says: He gives little and then stops. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, and He gave a little and he was given nothing he said: It was cut off so he was not given anything. Haven’t you seen the well called Akkad? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And his stipend was cut off. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Tawus and Qatadah, regarding his statement, and he gave a little, he said: He gave a little, then stopped that. He said: Ibn Thaur told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, something similar. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And he was stingy means he was stingy and his stinginess was cut off. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, and he was afflicted, meaning his stipend was cut off. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about his statement and akadda and Akada Asira and the Arabs say: So-and-so dug and akadda, and that is when he reached the kaddaa, which is when a man digs in the plain and then faces a mountain and he digs it. It is said that he has akadda, and his nails and fingers became thick and deficient, if they became thick and his fingers became tired and did not work at all, and the girl’s income is little, with a hamzah. Some of the people of knowledge of the Arabic language say that his statement akadda is derived from kaddaa which is that he digs until he despairs of water, so it is said at that time we have reached her kaddaa.
53:34: God Almighty says: And He gave little and was straitened.
53:35: And His statement: Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees? God Almighty says: Does this person, to whom his companion promised that he would bear God’s punishment on his behalf in the Hereafter, have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees the truth of his words and his fulfillment of what he promised him?
53:36: And His statement: Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses? God Almighty says: Or has this person not been informed that he will bear the punishment of God in the Hereafter because of what is in the scriptures of Moses, son of Imran, peace be upon him?
53:37: And his saying: And Abraham who fulfilled means: And Abraham who fulfilled what he was sent to. Then the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of who fulfilled. Some of them said that it was his fulfillment of what his Lord had entrusted him with, which was to convey His messages, which is: No soul shall bear the burden of another. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And Abraham who fulfilled. He said: Before Abraham, they used to take guardians to guardians until Abraham came and he reached: No soul shall bear the burden of another. No one shall be held accountable for the sin of another. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And Abraham who fulfilled he said: And fulfilled the obedience of God and conveyed the messages of his Lord to His creation. And Ikrimah used to say: And in these ten verses it says: No soul shall bear the burden of another… until he reached: And upon Him is the next life. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And Abraham who fulfilled in obeying God and His messages to His creation. Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told me: Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: And Abraham who fulfilled, he said: He conveyed what he was commanded to do. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan and Ibrahim who fulfilled, saying: He conveyed. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And Abraham who fulfilled, he said: He fulfilled and conveyed the messages of his Lord. He conveyed what he was sent with, just as a man conveys what he was sent with. Others said: Rather, he fulfilled what he saw in the dream of slaughtering his son. They said that his statement, No soul shall bear the burden of another is from the deferred meaning of the forward. They said: The meaning of the statement is, Or was he not informed of what is in the scrolls of Moses, ‘No soul shall bear the burden of another’, and what is in the scrolls of Abraham, who fulfilled. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My paternal uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses * and Abraham who fulfilled? He says: Abraham is the one who completed the obedience in what he did with his son when he saw the vision, and what is in the scriptures of Moses is, No soul shall bear the burden of another, to the end of the verse. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Lahi’ah told me on the authority of Abu Sakhr on the authority of Al-Qurazi, and he was asked about this verse: And Abraham who fulfilled. He said: He fulfilled his promise by sacrificing his son. Others said that this means that he fulfilled all the laws of Islam to his Lord. Who said that? Abdullah bin Ahmed bin Shabwa told us: Ali bin Al-Hassan told us: Kharijah bin Musaab told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Islam is thirty arrows, and no one was afflicted with this religion and established it except Abraham. God said, And Abraham who fulfilled, so God wrote for him a release from the Fire. Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And Abraham who fulfilled what was imposed upon him. Others said that he fulfilled what was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the hadith that... Abu Kurayb told us: Rashdin bin Saad told us: Ziyad bin Faid told us, on the authority of Sahl bin Muadh, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: Shall I not tell you why God called Abraham His faithful friend? Because he used to say every morning and evening: ‘Glory be to God when you go to bed at night and when you wake up in the morning,’ until he finished the verse.” Others said: Rather, he fulfilled his Lord’s daily work. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Al-Hasan bin Atiyah told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Ja`far bin Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And Abraham who fulfilled. He said: Do you know what he fulfilled? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: And in the work of his day, four rak`ahs during the day. The most correct of the statements on this matter is the statement of those who said: And in the laws of Islam and all that he commanded of obedience, because God Almighty mentioned that he fulfilled it, so the statement about his fulfilling it included all obedience and did not specify some over others. If someone were to say that he limited that to his statement, And in * that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, then that is something that God, the Most High, has informed us is in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham, not something that he limited the report to, that he fulfilled. As for the fulfillment, then it is general. Even if the two reports that we mentioned, or one of them, were authentic from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, we would not have attributed it to anyone else, but there is a problem with their chain of transmission, for which verification is necessary.
53:38: And his saying: No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, then from his saying no bearer of burdens according to the interpretation we have interpreted it is in the position of a genitive in response to what is in his saying Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses? He means by his saying no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another other than her, rather every sinner, then her sin is upon her. We have explained the interpretation of this based on the differences among scholars in what has passed before. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told us: Abu Malik Al-Janbi told us: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us on the authority of Abu Malik Al-Ghifari regarding his statement, No soul shall bear the burden of another, and that man shall have nothing but what he strives for, to His statement, of the first vows, he said, This is in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses. Rather, what he meant by his saying, No soul shall bear the burden of another, is what he guaranteed to Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira that he would bear the punishment of God on the Day of Resurrection. He says: Did not the one who said this statement and the one who guaranteed this guarantee inform us of what is written in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham that no sinner shall bear the sin of another and that man shall have nothing but what he strives for, and God Almighty says: Or did He not inform us that no worker will be rewarded except for his work, whether it be good or evil?
53:39: As Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And that man can have nothing but what he strives for, and he recited, Indeed, your striving is diverse (al-Layl 92:4), he said: Your deeds. It was reported on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said that this verse was abrogated. Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And that man can have nothing but what he strives for. He said: Then God revealed after this, And those who believe and whose offspring follow them in faith - We will join with them their offspring. (al-Tur 52:21) So the children will enter Paradise through the righteousness of their fathers.
53:40: His Most High saying: And that his effort will be seen. God Almighty says: And that the work of every worker will be seen on the Day of Resurrection from the time of Resurrection with the recompense for which he will be rewarded, whether good or evil. He will not be held accountable for the punishment of a sin other than that of his worker, nor will any worker other than him be rewarded for his good work. Rather, what is meant by that is the one who turned away from his Islam with his friend’s guarantee that he will bear the punishment on his behalf, that his guarantee will not benefit him or avail him at all on the Day of Resurrection, because every worker will be held accountable for his knowledge.
53:41: And His statement: Then He will reward him with the fullest reward. God Almighty says: Then he will be rewarded for his effort with that fullest reward. God Almighty only said the fullest because He fulfilled what He promised His creation for it in terms of reward. The ha in His statement, Then He will reward him is from the mention of the effort, and it returned to that.
53:42: And His statement: And to your Lord is the final destination. God Almighty says: To His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to your Lord, O Muhammad, is the final destination and return of all His creation. He is the One who will reward all of them for their deeds, the righteous and the wicked, the good and the evil.
53:43: And His statement: And that it is He who makes laugh and cry God Almighty says: And that your Lord is He who makes laugh the people of Paradise in Paradise by entering it and makes cry the people of Hell in Hell by entering it and makes laugh whomever He wants from the people of this world and makes cry whomever He wants to make cry from them.
53:44: God Almighty says that He is the One who caused death among His creation, and He gives life to those among them who live. What He meant by His saying gives life is the breathing of the soul into the dead sperm, making it alive by placing the soul in it.
53:45: And His statement, And that He created the two mates, the male and the female, from a sperm-drop when it is emitted, God Almighty says: And that He innovated the creation of the two mates, the male and the female, and made them two mates, because the male is the mate of the female and the female has a mate, so they are two mates, each of them being a mate for the other.
53:46: And His saying, from a sperm-drop when it is emitted, and from is a connection to creation. God Almighty says: He created that from a sperm-drop when the man and woman ejaculated.
53:47: And His statement, And that upon Him is the other creation, the Almighty says: And that your Lord, O Muhammad, will create these two pairs after their death and their trial in their graves with the other creation, and that is to bring them back to life as a new creation as they were before their death.
53:48: God Almighty says: And your Lord is richer than any of His creation in wealth and has provided him with wealth and made for him the means of obtaining wealth. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this verse. Some of them said what we said about it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Saleh, regarding his statement, enriched and satisfied, he said: enriched with money and satisfied with property. Others said about me, when he said, I am rich, that is, I serve. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Asim told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And that He is the One who enriches and provides, he said: Enriches is a master and provides: He serves. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us on the authority of Abu Raja’ on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, enriched and satisfied, he said: and served. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, enriched and satisfied, he said: enriched and served. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, enriched and satisfied, he said: gave, satisfied, and served. Others said that he meant that he was richer than money and satisfied. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And that He is the Most Rich and the Most Satisfied, he said: For He is the Most Rich and the Most Satisfied. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: And that He is the Most Enriching and the Most Satisfying. He said: The one who enriches and is satisfied means being pleased. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, enriched, he said: made him a master, and satisfied, he said: satisfied. Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And that He is the One who enriches and satisfies him, meaning: He gave him and satisfied him. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, like the hadith of Ibn Bashar, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Sufyan. Others said that he meant that he enriched himself and made his creation poorer to him. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us on the authority of his father: And that He is the richest and most content. He said: A Hadrami claimed that it was mentioned to him that He is the richest of himself and the poorest of creation to Him. Others said that he meant that he enriched whomever he wanted of his creation and impoverished whomever he wanted. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And that He is the Most Enriched and the Most Satisfied, he said: He enriched and increased, and He satisfied and decreased. And he recited, He expands provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him (Saba’: 36).
53:49: And His statement, And that He is the Lord of Sirius, God Almighty says: And that your Lord, O Muhammad, is the Lord of Sirius. He means by Sirius: the star called by this name, which is a star that some of the people of ignorance used to worship instead of God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And that He is the Lord of Sirius, he said, It is the star called Sirius. Ali bin Sahl told me: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And that He is the Lord of Sirius, he said: The planet behind Gemini, they used to worship it. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid: And that He is the Lord of Sirius. He said: It was worshipped in the pre-Islamic era. Muhammad bin Amr told us: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Lord of Sirius, he said: Marzam is the star of Gemini. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And that He is the Lord of Sirius, there was a tribe of Arabs who worshipped Sirius, this star that you saw. Bishr said: He means the star that follows Gemini. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, Lord of Sirius, that they used to worship this star called Sirius in the pre-Islamic era. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And that He is the Lord of Sirius, it was worshipped in the pre-Islamic period. So he said: Do you worship this and abandon its Lord? Worship its Lord. He said: Sirius is the blazing star that follows Gemini, and it is called Al-Mirzam.
53:50: And His statement, And that He destroyed the former ‘Aad, means that the former ‘Aad were ‘Aad, son of Iram, son of Aws, son of Sam, son of Noah, and they are the ones whom God destroyed with a furious, violent wind, and He meant them with His statement, Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with ‘Aad, Iram? (al-Fajr 89:6-7). The reciters differed in their recitation of this, so the majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the reciters of Basra recited it, leaving the hamza and jazm of the noon until the lam in al-ala became like a heavy lam. The Arabs do that in such a case. It was reported from them that they heard it from them. Qum because ‘anna means Qum now. They jazm the meem when the lam with the alif in al-an was moved. Likewise, you say Sam Ithnayn meaning Sam al-Ithnayn. As for the majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of the Meccans, they recited it by making the noon pronounced and kasra and jazm of the first letter, with differences in that from al-A’mash. His companions narrated from him, except for al-Qasim bin Ma’n, that he agreed with the people of his country in that. As for al-Qasim bin Ma’n, it was reported from al-A’mash that he agreed with the recitation of the Medinans in that. The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is what we mentioned from the Kufians, because that is the eloquent speech of the Arabs, and the reading of those who are people of natural disposition is based on clarity and emphasis, and assimilation in such a letter and leaving clarity is only permitted for those who have that in their nature and disposition from the people of the desert. As for those who are born, their rule is that they should seek out the most eloquent, sweetest, and most reliable readings, even if the other ones are permissible and not rejected. And it was said that Ad bin Iram was the first Ad because the sons of Luqaym bin Hazal bin Ubail bin Dhadd bin Ad the elder were, at the time when God sent His punishment upon Ad the elder, living in Mecca with their brothers from the Amalekites, the sons of Amalek bin Lawdh bin Sam bin Noah, and they were not with their people from Ad in their land, so the punishment that befell their people did not afflict them, and they are the Ad of the Hereafter, and then they perished after that. The destruction of the people of Ad in the Hereafter was due to the aggression of some of them against others, so they were killed in the killing. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, as we mentioned, that the greater ‘Ad, whose descendants God destroyed with the wind, was called the first ‘Ad because they were destroyed before the last ‘Ad. Ibn Zayd used to say: The first ‘Ad was called that because they were the first of the nations to be destroyed. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, He destroyed the first ‘Aad, that it is said: They are among the first nations.
53:51: And His statement, And Thamud - what did He leave behind? God Almighty says: God did not leave Thamud behind, leaving them in their transgression and rebellion against their Lord, but He punished them for their disbelief and insolence, so He destroyed them. The reciters differed in their reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Basra and some of the Kufians read it as and Thamud, so what did He leave in accordance with the procedure, following the Qur’an, since the alif was fixed in it. Some of the majority of the Kufians read it without the procedure, and it was mentioned that it is in the Qur’an of Abdullah without the alif. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings, so whichever one the reader recites is correct, because they are both correct in terms of grammar and meaning. We have explained the story of Thamud and the reason for their destruction previously, so there is no need to repeat it.
53:52: God Almighty says: And that He destroyed the people of Noah before them, Aad and Thamud. Indeed, they were more unjust to themselves, more disbelieving in their Lord, and more rebellious and disobedient to God than those nations whom He destroyed after them. And their rebellion was what God described them with, and they were thus more rebellious than other nations. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, “And the people of Noah before them. Indeed, they were more unjust and more rebellious.” There was no tribe of people more unjust and more rebellious than the people of Noah. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called them for a thousand years minus fifty years. Whenever a generation perished and a generation arose, the Prophet of God called them until he mentioned to us that a man would take his son by the hand and walk with him, saying, O my son, my father walked with me to this point, and I am like you, and I will be like you on that day, following one another in misguidance and denial of the command of God. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, Indeed, they were more unjust and more rebellious, he said, The Prophet of God called them for a thousand years minus fifty years.
53:53: And His statement, And the overturned city, I have cast it down. God Almighty says: And the city that was overturned, its top being its bottom, and it is the city of Sodom, the people of Lot, God cast it down, so He commanded Gabriel, peace and blessings be upon him, to lift it from the seventh earth with his wing, then He cast it down upside down. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, And the one that was overturned, He inclined. He said: Gabriel inclined it. He said: He raised it to the sky and then made it fall. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Ibn Isa Yahya Ibn Rafi’: And the overturned city I am falling into. He said: The village of Lot when I fall into it. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And the overturned city I incline towards, he said: The village of Lot. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And the overturned ones I desire, he said: They are the people of Lot. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement, And the overturned city, I cast down, that the village of Lot was brought down from the sky, then that rock followed it, uprooted from the earth, then he cast it down into the sky, then it was turned upside down. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And the overturned ones I incline towards, he said, The deniers, may God destroy them.
53:54: And His statement, And that which covered it covered it, God Almighty says: So God covered the overturned city with that which covered it, and He rained down upon it of baked clay. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And what covered it covered it covered it with layered rocks. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: What covered her covered her means: stones. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And that which covered them covered them, he said: The stones that He threw at them from the sky.
53:55: He says, Then which of the favors of your Lord do you dispute? God Almighty says: Then which of the favors of your Lord, O son of Adam, which He has bestowed upon you do you doubt, suspect, and argue? The favors are the plural of to, and there are three forms for the singular form: to, for example, on, and to, for example, on, and to, for example, ala. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Then which of the favors of your Lord do you dispute? He said: Then which of the favors of God do you dispute, O son of Adam? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: Then which of the favors of your Lord do you dispute? He said: Which of the favors of your Lord do you dispute?
53:56: And his saying, This is a warner among the first warners. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of His saying, may His praise be exalted, to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, This is a warner among the first warners, and His description of him as being among the first warners and the last of them. Some of them said: The meaning of that is that he is a warner to his people, and the warners who came before him were warners to their people, just as one says: This is one of the children of Adam and one of the people. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, This is a warner among the first warners, he said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was warned just as the messengers before him were warned. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, This is a warner among the first warners, that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent with what the messengers before him were sent with. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Ja`far: This is a warner from the first warners. He said: He is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Others said that the meaning of this is different from all of this and they said: Its meaning is this that I warned you of, O people, from the events that I mentioned to you that I brought about with the nations before you from the warnings that I warned the nations before you in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Malik: This is a warning from the first warnings. He said: Among the things with which they warned their people in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses. What I mentioned about Abu Malik is more similar to the interpretation of the verse, and that is that God Almighty mentioned it in the context of the verses that He informed us about, which are in the scrolls of Abraham and Moses, and a warner from the first warners that came to the nations before you, just as they came to you. So his saying, This is to be a reference to what preceded it in speech, is more appropriate and similar to something else.
53:57: And his saying, The approaching event has drawn near, means: The approaching event has drawn near. What he means is that the Resurrection has drawn near to you, O people. It is said from this that the departure of so-and-so has drawn near, as Nabigha of Banu Dhubyan said: The departure time has come, but our passengers have not yet left our saddlebags, as if they had As Kaab bin Zuhair said: Youth has passed and gray hair has come, and I see no successor to the departing youth. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The approaching hour has drawn near. One of the names of the Day of Resurrection is the greatness of God and His warning to His servants. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The approaching hour has drawn near, he said, The Hour has drawn near. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, The approaching hour has drawn near, that it is the Hour, for which there is none to avert but God.
53:58: And His statement, There is none to avert it besides God. God the Almighty says: The approaching Hour, which is the Hour that has drawn near, has none to avert it besides God. He says, it will not be revealed and come to pass except by God establishing it and revealing it without anyone else from His creation, because no close angel or sent prophet has seen it. It was said, Kashfah, but it was made feminine, and it means uncovering, as was said, Do you see for them any remainder? (al-Haqqah 69:8), meaning do you see for them any remainder? And as was said, The outcome, and what it has of a deterrent; and as was said, There is no denier of its occurrence (al-Waqi’ah 56:2), meaning denial; And it will not cease to uncover treachery among them. (al-Ma’idah 5:13), meaning treachery.
53:59: God Almighty says to the polytheists of Quraysh 106:“O people, is it this Qur’an that you are amazed at, that it was sent down to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that you laugh at it in mockery of it and do not cry because of what it contains of threats to those who disobey God, while you are among those who disobey Him?” And you are heedless means leave us alone with your amusement. It is said from it samd “samud” meaning, to be heedless. And in a similar manner to what we have said about this, the people of interpretation said, although their expressions differed regarding it. Some of them said, Heedless, some of them said, Enriched, and some of them said, Distracted. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, samidun, he said: It is singing. When they heard the Qur’an, they would sing and play, and it is the language of the people of Yemen. The Yemeni said: Asmad. Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Samidon, meaning: heedless. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And you are heedless, meaning: distracted. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: She is a Yemeni woman, Asmad, singing for us. Abu Kuraib told us: Al-Ashja’i told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It is singing, and it is Yemeni. They say, Sing for us, and we will sing for you. He said: Ubaidullah Al-Ashja’i narrated to us on the authority of Sufyan on the authority of Hakim bin Al-Daylam on the authority of Al-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And you are standing tall. He said: They would pass by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, standing tall. Have you not seen the stallion among the camels, standing tall and proud? Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement, And you are heedless, he said: Heedless. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And you are steadfast. He said: They would pass by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, angry and gloating. Ikrimah said: It is singing in the Himyarite dialect. He said: Al-Ashja’i and Waki’ narrated to us on the authority of Sufyan on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid who said: It is the bartama. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And you are steadfast, he said: The Bartama. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Abu Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And you are steadfast, he said: The Bartama. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Samidun are the singers in the Himyarite dialect. Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Ikrimah used to say: The Samidun sing in the Himyarite dialect, and Ibn Abbas is not in it. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Samidun meaning heedless. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, Samidun, he said: Heedless. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: Regarding His statement, and you are idling, idling means amusement and play. Humaid bin Masada told us: Yazid bin Zari’ told us: Sufyan bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Fitr, on the authority of Abu Khalid al-Walabi, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: He saw them standing, waiting for the Imam, so he said: What is wrong with you, why are you standing? Ibn Sinan Al-Qazzaz told me: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Imran bin Zaida bin Nasheet, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Khalid, who said: Ali, may God be pleased with him, came out to us while we were standing and said: Why do I see you standing? He said: Abu Asim told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Fitr, on the authority of Zaida, on the authority of Abu Khalid, something similar. Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement, And you are staying up, he said, standing at night before the imam comes. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Imran al-Khayyat, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding the people waiting for the prayer while standing. He said: It was said that was the Samud. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Layth and Al-Azrami, on the authority of Mujahid: And you are steadfast. He said: The burtum. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And you are steadfast. He said: Singing in Yemeni means sing for us. Yunus told us: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And you are heedless. He said, Heedless means heedless. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: They used to hate to stand when the muezzin called for prayer and the imam was not with them, and they used to hate to wait for him to stand, and it was said: That is the samud or from the samud.
53:60: God Almighty says: And you laugh and do not cry.
53:61: And God Almighty said, And you are steadfast.
53:62: And His statement, So prostrate to God and worship Him, God Almighty says: So prostrate to God, O people, in your prayers, without any other gods or rivals besides Him, and worship Him alone, for worship should not be for anyone but Him, so devote your worship and prostration to Him and do not make any partner for Him in your worship of Him.
